Sep 5OUTBOUND DAYMedium confidenceSep 5 · 18:00–22:00 ET
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.
NWS-hr
NWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.
NWS-day
NWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. A GFS MAV MOS row corroborates the flight category on this day.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. This day is already covered by finer-resolution sources.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Short term

.. (This evening through Sunday) Issued at 359 PM EDT Sat Sep 5 2026 Heat Concerns Continue: Current satellite loop shows scattered clouds developing across the area with some showers and thunderstorms across North and Central GA. Very warm temps continue across the area with highs expected in the middle to upper 90s through the short term. With dewpoints in the 70s we can expect to see Heat Index values in the 103 to 109 deg range Today and Sunday. Have extended the heat advisory to include Sunday which should be our last day of these extreme temps (at least through the next 7 days). Severe Thunderstorms Possible This Weekend: The Bermuda ridge that kept us mostly dry for most of this past week is finally weakening as the next frontal boundary nears the area from the NE. This weakening ridge is allowing typical scattered summertime pop-up showers and storms to develop across central GA, where moisture has pooled and subsidence from the fleeting ridge is lower. The second area for storms is across north/northeast GA associated with increased moisture ahead of the approaching cold front which is pushing SW down the eastern seaboard and should move into NE GA between 12z-18z Sun. Scattered strong to severe storms are possible, with the primary threat being damaging wind gusts, and frequent lightning strikes. SPC has the aforementioned corridor of north/northeast GA in a Marginal Risk (Level 1 of 5) for severe weather with a Severe Thunderstorm watch just N and E of our area across portions of the Carolinas. On Sunday, convective activity will ramp up even more, as a shortwave and associated frontal boundary start to move across the area. This forcing, combined with the warm and humid airmass in place out ahead of it, will support scattered to numerous afternoon showers and storms, with generally higher coverage across central GA. Several storms may be strong to severe, with damaging wind gusts, and frequent lightning strikes as the primary threats. The greatest risk for severe storms will be across portions of east and Central GA, where SPC has a Slight Risk (Level 2 of 5) for severe weather. With the potential for repeated rounds of storms and efficient rainfall rates, we'll also have to watch out for localized flash flooding, especially in urban and poor-drainage areas.

Long term

.. (Monday morning through next Friday) Issued at 359 PM EDT Sat Sep 5 2026 By Monday and the start of the long term, mid-level ridging situated across the midsection of the country will begin migrating eastward. Chances for showers and thunderstorms will largely be focused along the front (which may slow down or speed up as we approach the short term), the best of which (60-80%) appear to be across the far southeastern portion of the forecast area. Sensible effects of the front will be fairly substantial given the preceding heat, with highs as much as 8-10 degrees "cooler" (relatively speaking) than Sunday -- in the lower 80s to lower 90s. Portions of northeast Georgia at elevation may even remain in the 70s. Expect further fine tuning of Monday's temperatures as they're directly tied to frontal progress. Tuesday and beyond, the core of the aforementioned mid-level ridging will move overhead, accompanied by high pressure at the surface -- oriented such that we're likely to have an extended period of "cold" air damming. Heat will begin to build once again, with highs returning to several degrees above average by mid-to-late week. Breezy easterly winds should support ample mixing during the afternoon, which will initially serve to keep heat index values within a few degrees of air temperatures. Widespread convective development will be hampered by subsidence, with rain chances relegated largely to portions of south central Georgia through Wednesday. The presiding mid-level ridge will retrograde westward across the Four Corners region on Thursday, allowing for more substantial moisture intrusion across the Southeast, and a return to more uniform afternoon thunderstorm chances areawide.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KAVL observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSSI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJZI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHXD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSAV is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KROA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSGJ observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KFIN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGKT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTYS is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KECP observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KPNS observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJKA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBFM observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSPG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KPIE is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTPA is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KVNC observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSRQ is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHSA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial). This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KGPT is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. A TAF was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. A station-calibrated GFS MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: partial).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: AUTH_ERROR), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

A raster chart may be displayed with its issuing office and valid time. No category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go on this page is derived from, or attributed to, an image. If retrieval fails the slot says UNAVAILABLE; it is never left blank.

3 · Hazard feeds & regional observations

Unfiltered hazard feeds (not route-geometry screened): 23 SIGMET records, 25 G-AIRMET records, 7 CWA records. Regional current observations (not corridor forecasts): no adverse or unknown current categories identified.
Scope: Hazard counts are raw feed totals and have not been filtered against a proposed route, altitude, or time. Airport flight categories are current point observations, not corridor forecasts.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

Executive summaryDeterministic · restates page evidence · no model called

A plain restatement of evidence shown in full below, computed from that evidence with no model call. It reports what the sources say; it does not rank the days, rate them, or make a go/no-go call. It follows the order the owner asked for: feasibility evidence, KLZU, destinations, weather by area or region, then new KLZU NOTAMs.

1 · Feasibility evidence for the trip window

This part is a derivation, not an observation: it states how much of the trip window carries a forecast flight category, and nothing more. It is not a go/no-go call, not a recommendation, and not a flight category. Its inputs and its gaps are listed in the tooltip on the line below.

  • Trip window: Fri Sep 4 – Mon Sep 7, 2026. “This weekend” is taken to mean exactly this window; no other date range is assessed.
  • Trip-window feasibility evidence (Derived): assessable for every active trip day — 3 of 3 active trip days in Fri Sep 4 – Mon Sep 7, 2026 carry a forecast flight category and 0 carry none. This is a derived statement about how much evidence exists, it is not a flight category, and it says nothing about whether a flight is advisable. Every input and every gap is named in this line's tooltip.

2 · KLZU home-base status

The KLZU observation and the per-day board categories, taken from the same helpers the board itself renders from, so the two cannot disagree.

  • KLZU current observation: VFR — from the surface observation read this run; it describes conditions now, not a trip day.
  • Sat Sep 5, 18:00–22:00 ET: VFR — most restrictive forecast flight category; medium confidence; from MOS.
  • Sun Sep 6, 06:00–22:00 ET: VFR — most restrictive forecast flight category; medium confidence; from MOS.
  • Mon Sep 7, 06:00–22:00 ET: MVFR — most restrictive forecast flight category; medium confidence; from MOS.
  • A forecast flight category is available for 3 of 3 active trip days; 0 reach no category-capable product at this lead time.
  • Data quality: DEGRADED — as reported by the badge in the page header; it gates publication, it is not a weather statement.

3 · Destination coverage

Coverage, not a pick: this counts which destinations a product permitted to state a flight category actually reaches. It is not a ranking, not a recommendation, and the editorial order of the destination list is not a flyability score.

  • Destinations: 29 of 29 covered airports resolve a forecast flight category on at least one active trip day; 0 resolve none at this lead time. Counted from the same per-day outlook the destination cards render, with outlook-grade blocks excluded.

5 · New KLZU NOTAMs

This run keeps no snapshot of the previous run, so “new” cannot mean “changed since last time”. It is defined below as an FAA-published timestamp window, and the service-status scan reads the published text of every KLZU record so a status embedded inside a record of another category is not missed.

  • Baseline for “new”: a KLZU NOTAM whose own FAA-published timestamp (last update, else issue, else effective start) falls within the 72 hours before this run's generation time (2026-09-05T22:57:58.514862+00:00). This run holds no copy of the previous run's NOTAM set, so this is a source-timestamp window and not a difference against an earlier run.
  • KLZU NOTAM query state is AUTH_ERROR, so this run does not know the KLZU NOTAM picture. No new NOTAM count is stated: an incomplete query is not the same as no NOTAMs.

This restates evidence; it is not a recommendation, not an all-clear, and not a data outage. The decision surfaces are the planning gates and the ForeFlight cross-check below, read against the KLZU board and destination cards. Every line above restates a value shown elsewhere on this page.

Everything the page does

  • Mission Control with destination and day selection, fail-closed category ranges, a keyboard- and touch-operable schematic airport map, filters, clustering, and a synchronized text list
  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Current-and-future KLZU board with four fixed 06:00–22:00 ET boxes and outbound/return day context
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the visible standard box — a box with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Published PDF download plus browser print fallback — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS owner-approved production source NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; reporting an explicit error state rather than an empty list, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
